events.text: The overview: cropland analysed, black soil, heavy damage, people on damaged land
Where to start: the map coloured by priority, and the top areas
Any analysed month: the Atlas runs every month by itself
Near term or post-crisis: two ways to rank the same land
Next steps, worked out from the data: tick them off for the team
A budget: the hectares it covers are worked out again
The map: priority square by square, with the states' names and borders
Colour the map by value, by damage, by feasibility, or all together
Macro: whole states ranked; Micro: every square
Satellite only: the land itself under the squares
Move the weights: the map recolours and the top areas move at once
The feasibility cutoff leaves out the least reachable land for now, with a soft edge
A place's details: its scores, soil types, hectares, people and recovery cost
Data: every analysed month; hover a bar for its numbers
Heavily damaged land, new damage or people, month by month
Compare two months: what changed, and the squares that changed most
The report: the totals, the top ten places, the settings and this month's alerts
Save as PDF for donors, or download every square as a spreadsheet
The assistant: ask about any place; it answers from the same numbers as the map
A saved conversation about one top area
Settings: the areas, the crisis, the data and the team
A new area: a country or region, GPS coordinates, or a drawn shape
The last twelve months are analysed; the area joins the list and the map
The team: who can see this area and who can change it
The crisis: the app's list of wars, a date your team sets, a natural disaster, or none
